title: Words on breaking the fast
cue: What the Prophet ﷺ said when he broke his fast
arabic: ذَهَبَ الظَّمَأُ وَابْتَلَّتِ الْعُرُوقُ وَثَبَتَ الْأَجْرُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
translation: The thirst has gone, the veins are moist, and the reward is assured, if Allah wills.

gradings.in: Sunan al-Daraqutni, Kitab al-Siyam, after hadith 2279 (Mu’assasat al-Risala edition)
gradings.quote: تفرد به الحسين بن واقد وإسناده حسن

witnesses.name: shamela
witnesses.ref: Sunan Abi Dawud, ed. Muhyi al-Din Abd al-Hamid, vol. 2 p. 306, no. 2357 (shamela.ws/book/1726/3158)

provenance.note: The Arabic stored is the supplication only. In Abu Dawud it follows the frame “the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he broke his fast, used to say”, which is given here in the cue and the usage line, not in the Arabic.

notes.text: Al-Nawawi quotes the second wording from Abu Dawud, where Mu’adh ibn Zuhrah says it reached him that the Prophet ﷺ used to say it on breaking his fast, and remarks that he narrated it like this, [[mursal]].

when: On breaking the fast at sunset

variants.label: Another wording, from a mursal report: “O Allah, for You I have fasted, and on Your provision I break my fast.”
variants.arabic: اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ صُمْتُ وَعَلَى رِزْقِكَ أَفْطَرْتُ

citations.narrator: Mu’adh ibn Zuhrah, who says it reached him
